findings.title: Student performance GET path recomputes and writes every class snapshot
findings.rationale: A student opening the summary causes per-class recomputation instead of reading the already-persisted snapshots. Cost and write contention scale with enrollment count, and the GET path can emit domain events and logs.
findings.evidence: getStudentOwnSummary maps every active enrollment through recomputeStudent. Each recomputation performs two component reads sequentially, reads the existing snapshot, updates or inserts it, and may read intervention state and write a performance log.
findings.expectedImpact: Make the common read path predictable and reduce database reads, writes, lock pressure, duplicate events, and latency fan-out.
findings.verificationTarget: Add a query-count regression test for getStudentOwnSummary and prove the common path is read-only; preserve event-driven snapshot refresh tests.

findings.title: AI process lifecycle owns untracked background work and leaks during tests
findings.rationale: Untracked create_task extraction work is lost on restart and is not awaited or cancelled at shutdown. The test process also reproduces a stuck executor teardown, making failures expensive and CI unreliable.
findings.evidence: Two extraction routes schedule _run() with create_task while newer intervention, quiz, and lesson-plan flows explicitly delegate execution to BullMQ. Full tests emitted an executor thread join warning after 300 seconds; tests.test_backend_uploads passed assertions but did not terminate within 10 seconds when run as a module.
findings.expectedImpact: Reliable shutdown, bounded concurrency, restart-safe extraction jobs, faster tests, and one consistent backend-owned queue model.
findings.verificationTarget: A targeted extraction queue contract test, shutdown test with no pending tasks/threads, and an AI suite timeout below a documented threshold.

findings.title: Critical CI workloads have no timeout despite reproducible hangs
findings.rationale: A hanging build or test can consume a runner until the platform default timeout, delaying feedback and hiding the actual failing subsystem.
findings.evidence: Frontend build remained at optimized build creation for several minutes; frontend Jest reported open handles; AI tests exceeded five minutes. The corresponding CI jobs have no timeout-minutes guard.
findings.expectedImpact: Fail-fast feedback, bounded machine usage, and clearer separation of code failures from lifecycle failures.
findings.verificationTarget: CI jobs terminate at explicit subsystem budgets and upload the last diagnostic output on timeout.

findings.title: Class-record writes and section reads fan out per row or class
findings.rationale: Bulk score updates launch one upsert per student without a concurrency bound, while adviser-section results issue one query per class. Larger sections multiply database round trips and pool pressure.
findings.evidence: bulkRecordScores uses Promise.all over dto.scores with an individual insert/on-conflict query; listAdviserSection uses Promise.all over class IDs with an individual classRecords query.
findings.expectedImpact: Fewer round trips, bounded pool usage, and more atomic bulk updates.
findings.verificationTarget: Existing class-record performance specs plus query-count assertions for representative section sizes and atomicity tests.

findings.title: Academic rollover clones nested assets through long serial insert loops
findings.rationale: The rare workflow is allowed to be slower than requests, but nested assessment, question, lesson, module, and section inserts can create a very long transaction and hold locks as content volume grows.
findings.evidence: cloneClassLearningAssets contains nested for/await insert sequences for assessments/questions/options and lessons/blocks, plus serial module and section inserts. The module has no nearby spec in the inventory.
findings.expectedImpact: Shorter rollover transactions and a clear scaling ceiling without changing academic semantics.
findings.verificationTarget: Fixture-based rollover benchmark at small/medium/large content volumes, rollback test, and exact cloned-count assertions.

findings.title: Frontend effects and timeout races create avoidable render and handle pressure
findings.rationale: State derived synchronously inside effects causes extra render passes, while Promise.race timers are not cancelled when the primary request wins. This is consistent with the open-handle warning from Jest.
findings.evidence: ESLint flags synchronous setState in SystemInfoButton and TeacherClassRecordWorkbook. AuthProvider creates an uncancelled timeout for every current-user race; the frontend suite reports asynchronous operations left open.
findings.expectedImpact: Cleaner render scheduling, fewer stale timers, faster test shutdown, and lower risk of state updates after navigation/unmount.
findings.verificationTarget: Targeted component/provider tests under fake timers, eslint clean for production files, and Jest exits without the open-handle warning.

findings.title: Several subsystem boundaries have collapsed into multi-thousand-line owners
findings.rationale: Adding one feature requires editing giant orchestration owners with many unrelated responsibilities, which magnifies merge conflicts and the chance that a local edit changes distant behavior.
findings.evidence: Largest owners include lxp.service.ts at 6352 lines, assessments.service.ts at 5350, ai-mentor.controller.ts at 2844, AI main.py at 5420 with more than 50 route decorators, and the teacher class page at 4453 with 15 effect callbacks.
findings.expectedImpact: Smaller blast radii, clearer ownership, targeted tests, and safer incremental extension.
findings.verificationTarget: Characterization tests around extracted boundaries; no route, DTO, response-envelope, or authorization changes during decomposition.

findings.title: Large lint baselines obscure new correctness and performance signals
findings.rationale: Thousands of existing warnings and advisory lint jobs make it difficult to distinguish a newly introduced unsafe access, empty cleanup path, or React performance error from historical debt.
findings.evidence: Backend lint reports 5228 findings and frontend lint reports 71. CI intentionally continues on lint error for both subsystems.
findings.expectedImpact: Prevent new debt immediately while paying down old debt in bounded waves rather than attempting a destabilizing all-at-once cleanup.
findings.verificationTarget: Diff-aware lint gate or frozen baseline count, then per-module cleanup with build/tests after each wave.

findings.title: Storage cleanup failures are silently discarded
findings.rationale: S3 migration/upload succeeds even if the local file cannot be deleted, but the failure is invisible and can accumulate disk usage over time.
findings.evidence: Both saveFileRecord and saveUploadedFile use empty catch blocks around fs.promises.unlink; these are two of the three backend lint errors.
findings.expectedImpact: Detectable cleanup failures and bounded local disk growth without failing an otherwise successful remote upload.
findings.verificationTarget: Mock unlink failure, assert a structured warning/metric, and preserve successful upload response semantics.

findings.title: Mobile scope documentation contradicts the implemented role architecture
findings.rationale: Future agents are instructed to preserve a student-only app even though teacher/admin role resolution and teacher navigation are live. That can cause valid code to be removed or audits to miss half the app.
findings.evidence: mobile/AGENTS.md states the app is student-scoped; AppNavigator exposes TeacherNavigator/TeacherTabs and resolveMobileRole returns admin, teacher, or student.
findings.expectedImpact: Correct routing of future maintenance work and explicit ownership for role-specific mobile surfaces.
findings.verificationTarget: Update the product/slice contract after a user decision and keep role-resolution plus navigation manifest tests green.

findings.title: Runtime dependencies emit deprecation warnings in verified test paths
findings.rationale: Warnings are not current failures, but leaving them unresolved increases upgrade risk and hides more useful diagnostics.
findings.evidence: Backend tests report a legacy Winston transport warning for LokiTransport; AI tests report Starlette TestClient deprecation for the installed httpx integration.
findings.expectedImpact: Cleaner diagnostics and less disruptive future upgrades.
findings.verificationTarget: Isolated dependency compatibility branches with full affected-subsystem suites; do not mix these upgrades into performance fixes.

findings.title: High-consequence modules lack nearby characterization specs
findings.rationale: The safest way to reduce giant services and batch database work is to lock behavior first; missing module-local specs make even small refactors harder to prove.
findings.evidence: The inventory reports zero specs for academic-state, analytics, audit, rag, teacher, and additional small modules despite rollover, reporting, and AI boundary responsibilities.
findings.expectedImpact: Safer staged refactors and lower probability that a one-line change cascades through academic or AI flows.
findings.verificationTarget: Characterization tests for public service methods and contract-focused tests before refactoring each uncovered module.

safeImmediateFixes: Make the AI test entrypoint declare AI_RUNTIME_MODE=test and add explicit shutdown checks for clients, tasks, and default-executor work.
Add explicit CI timeout-minutes budgets to frontend and AI jobs and preserve diagnostic output on timeout.
Replace empty unlink catches with structured warnings/metrics while preserving successful upload semantics.
Fix the two production React set-state-in-effect findings and cancel AuthProvider timeout races after the winning branch completes.
Fix the three backend lint errors and establish a no-new-errors gate without attempting to clear 5225 warnings in one change.
Document the current mobile role scope once the product owner confirms teacher/admin mobile support is intentional.
conditionalRefactors: Change student performance summary to read existing snapshots and queue/recompute only missing or explicitly stale entries; keep the existing response envelope and event semantics.
Batch class-record score upserts and adviser-section reads, protected by query-count, atomicity, and existing performance specs.
Move extraction and retry execution from FastAPI create_task into the existing backend BullMQ orchestration pattern used by lesson-plan, quiz, and intervention jobs.
Add an academic rollover scale fixture and then batch only independent inserts while preserving foreign-key order and transaction rollback.
Decompose giant owners behind compatibility facades: backend read/query services, FastAPI routers plus job services, and frontend route-local hooks/components. Keep each extraction behavior-neutral.
deferredItems: A shared generated API contract package across backend, web, and mobile; this needs an explicit contract-change proposal and consumer migration plan.
Any new cache or persisted derived-data policy; measure query latency and staleness tolerance before introducing it.
Major Starlette/httpx or Winston/Loki transport upgrades; isolate them from performance remediation.
A decision on whether mobile is student-only or a multi-role product; documentation and architecture should follow that product decision.
